title: Animate the filter with a view transition
prompt:
Clicking **Hide sold-out** hides two cards instantly. Make the change animate:

1. Give every `.session-card` a **unique** `view-transition-name` (in CSS, in JS, or both).
2. Run the filter update inside `document.startViewTransition()`, and fall back to a plain update when the method doesn't exist.
3. Make every `::view-transition-group` animation last **250ms**.
4. Turn the view-transition animations off for users who prefer reduced motion.

The checks spy on `document.startViewTransition` and also delete it to test your fallback.
hints: One CSS rule can read a per-card custom property: `view-transition-name: var(--vt-name);`. Set `--vt-name` per card from its id in JS.
In the click handler: `if (!document.startViewTransition) { applyFilter(); return; }` then `document.startViewTransition(() => applyFilter());`.
`::view-transition-group(*) { animation-duration: 250ms; }`, and inside `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` set `animation: none !important` on the group, old and new pseudo-elements.
explanation: Each card now has a unique name (`card-s1`, `card-s2`…), so the browser pairs its old and new snapshots and slides the remaining cards into the gaps while the hidden ones fade out. A shared name would make the browser skip the transition. Wrapping `applyFilter()` in `startViewTransition()` gives the browser its before and after states; the feature check keeps the button working in browsers without the API. The group animations are normal CSS animations, so `animation-duration` sets their timing and `animation: none` inside the reduced-motion query turns them into an instant change.

checks.unique-names: Every card has a unique view-transition-name
checks.uses-view-transition: The click runs the update inside startViewTransition()
checks.filter-works: Sold-out cards are hidden and the button state updates
checks.fallback-works: The button still works without the View Transition API
checks.reduced-motion: The animation is removed for reduced motion
